issues.text: A later study of blue plates in 18 people with dementia did not show a clear increase in eating.
issues.problem: The 18-person study is presented as a plain null result for blue plates. Its design deliberately put many pale, low-contrast foods on white-versus-blue plates, which is the reason the review gives for the difference from Dunne. Without that, a reader takes it as blue plates failing in general. The result is also reported only via the review (primary paper not opened).
issues.source_says: Gaffney 2026 full text: Donnelly et al. used a menu cycle with an increased frequency of low-contrast foods such as white rice and mashed potato; 28% of participants increased intake by at least 10%; the review reports no significant improvement with blue dishware in meals containing low-contrast foods and says colour alone may not be sufficient.
issues.replacement: A later study of blue plates in 18 people with dementia, on a menu with many pale foods such as white rice and mashed potato, did not show a clear increase in eating.

issues.text: Red plates for people with dementia come from a study of nine men
issues.problem: Origin claim: nothing in the evidence shows that the popular red plate tip derives from this study (the record says not to call it 'best-known' and to say it is the study that tested red tableware). Bluesky has the same wording ('Red plates for dementia come from a study of nine men').
issues.source_says: Dunne 2004 tested red tableware in nine men with advanced Alzheimer's disease; the abstract says nothing about being the source of the practice.
issues.replacement: The 2004 study that tested red plates for people with dementia had nine men

issues.text: Red plates for dementia come from a study of nine men with advanced Alzheimer's:
issues.problem: Same unverifiable origin claim as the other platforms.
issues.source_says: As above.

issues.text: None was randomised and none lasted more than a month.
issues.problem: The review says study timeframes were not consistently reported; what it states is that the longest test period was 30 days. 'None lasted more than a month' asserts something about all four.
issues.source_says: Gaffney 2026: 'Study timeframes and intervention periods were not consistently reported across all studies, with the longest test period lasting 30 days.'
issues.replacement: None was randomised, and the longest test period was 30 days.

issues.text: The researchers watched their meals for 10 days on white plates and cups
issues.problem: Dunne measured grams of food and ounces of liquid (weighed intake), not watched meals.
issues.source_says: Dunne 2004: dependent variables were amount of food (grams) and liquid (ounces); the review says weighed measures were used.
issues.replacement: The researchers weighed what the men ate for 10 days on white plates and cups

issues.text: A 2026 systematic review looked for every study of contrast at mealtimes and found four
issues.problem: 'Every study' claims completeness; the review searched five databases to March 2025 and included English-language studies only.
issues.source_says: Gaffney 2026: five databases searched from inception to March 2025; English only; four studies (five reports) included.
issues.replacement: A 2026 systematic review searched five databases up to March 2025 for studies of contrast at mealtimes and found four

issues.text: and in year two pneumonia was slightly more common in programme homes.
issues.problem: In the trial this was a non-significant rise. The X version drops the qualifier (LinkedIn has it), so a reader could take it as a signal of harm.
issues.source_says: Zimmerman 2020: 'In the second year, the rate of pneumonia was nonsignificantly higher in intervention NHs.'
issues.replacement: and in year two pneumonia was slightly, but not clearly, more common in programme homes.

issues.text: Two small trials suggested fewer pneumonia deaths at two years, with low certainty.
issues.problem: Omits the part of the Cochrane finding that points the other way, which the safe wording carried: a larger study found no clear difference in pneumonia deaths at 18 months. As written the Cochrane summary leans towards benefit.
issues.source_says: Cao 2022: low-certainty evidence from two studies (454 participants) of fewer pneumonia-associated deaths at 24 months (RR 0.43); 'Another study (2513 participants) reported insufficient evidence of a difference for this outcome at 18 months'.
issues.replacement: Two small trials suggested fewer pneumonia deaths at two years, with low certainty; a larger study found no clear difference at 18 months.

issues.text: Two small Japanese trials suggested fewer pneumonia deaths at two years, with low certainty.
issues.problem: Same omission of the larger study with no clear difference at 18 months.
issues.source_says: Cao 2022 abstract, as above.
issues.replacement: Two small Japanese trials suggested fewer pneumonia deaths at two years, with low certainty, but a larger study (2,513 people) found no clear difference in pneumonia deaths at 18 months.

issues.text: Two small trials: fewer pneumonia deaths at 2 years (low certainty)
issues.problem: Same omission; also repeated in the alt text.
issues.source_says: Cao 2022 abstract, as above.
issues.replacement: Two small trials: fewer pneumonia deaths at 2 years (low certainty); a larger study: no clear difference at 18 months

issues.text: The authors link the fade to the difficulty of keeping the programme going, and suggest dedicated oral care aides may be needed.
issues.problem: The authors say only that the lack of significant results in year two 'may be associated with sustainability'. 'Link the fade to' states a firmer cause than they do.
issues.source_says: Zimmerman 2020: 'The lack of significant results in the second year may be associated with sustainability. Improving mouth care in US NHs may require the presence and support of dedicated oral care aides.'
issues.replacement: The authors suggest the lack of a clear result in year two may relate to difficulty sustaining the programme, and that dedicated oral care aides may be needed.

issues.text: No trial compared mouth care with no mouth care: each compared extra, professional care with usual care.
issues.problem: This is the Cochrane review's classification, but the post has just named Yoneyama 2002, whose own abstract calls its control a 'no oral care group'. Unattributed, the sentence reads as contradicting the trial the post cites.
issues.source_says: Cao 2022: 'No studies evaluated oral care versus no oral care'; Yoneyama 2002 abstract: 'randomly assigned to an oral care group or a no oral care group'.
issues.replacement: The Cochrane review found no trial that compared mouth care with no mouth care: it classed each as extra, professional care against usual care.

issues.text: Small detail, real effect
issues.problem: Kicker claims a real effect. The post itself says no study tested whether opening packs changes how much people eat; the studies show only that many packs are hard to open and that bed posture needs more pinch strength.
issues.source_says: Bell 2016, 2013, 2017: difficulty opening packs and laboratory pinch strength and dexterity; no intake or outcome measured.
issues.replacement: Small detail, worth checking

issues.text: Four in ten healthy people over 65 could not open a hospital cheese portion
issues.problem: Stated as a flat count in the headline. The source says 39%, which cannot be a whole number of 40 people, so the denominator is unclear; and the Australian, community-volunteer setting is absent from the first line (Bluesky has it later).
issues.source_says: Bell 2016: 'Ten percent of the sample could not open the water bottles and 39% could not open cheese portions' (40 well people over 65 from 3 community settings, NSW).
issues.replacement: About four in ten healthy people over 65 could not open a hospital cheese portion

issues.text: "Difficult" is what they said, not a count of failures.
issues.problem: The 2013 study used interviews, questionnaires, observation and grip testing; the abstract does not say 'found difficult' came only from self-report, so this claim about method is unsupported.
issues.source_says: Bell 2013: 'found difficult to open by at least 40% of patients'; data from interviews, questionnaires, observations and grip strength testing.
issues.replacement: "Difficult" is not the same as a count of people who could not open them.

issues.text: 4. Opening a pack lying in bed takes more finger strength than sitting in a chair
issues.problem: Drops the population: this was a laboratory test in 34 well older volunteers, not patients. Same in the alt text.
issues.source_says: Bell 2017: n = 34 well older community-dwelling adults; laboratory study; 'Lying in a hospital bed required greater pinch strength and dexterity to open packs'.
issues.replacement: 4. In a lab test of 34 well older adults, opening a pack lying in bed took more finger strength than sitting in a chair

issues.text: 4: opening a pack lying in bed takes more finger strength than sitting in a chair.
issues.problem: Same population omission as the visual text.
issues.source_says: Bell 2017, as above.
issues.replacement: 4: in a lab test of 34 well older adults, opening a pack lying in bed took more finger strength than sitting in a chair.

issues.text: One result needs care. With the extra help, 56 in 100 residents kept or gained weight, against 28 in 100 in usual care, but most of that came from snacks between meals rather than from help at meals.
issues.problem: Two problems. (1) The population is missing: residents with low intake who had responded to a two-day trial of the help, not nursing home residents generally. (2) 'Most of that came from snacks' is not a finding about weight. The paper says three in four participants were assigned to snacks, so most of the gain in estimated calories was due to snacks; weight was not split by type of help, and residents were assigned to snacks when snacks gave them the larger calorie gain.
issues.source_says: Simmons 2008 full text: 56% maintained or gained weight on intervention vs 28% on control (crossover, 76 residents with low intake responsive to the 2-day trial); 'Of the 76 unique participants who completed intervention, 19 (25%) received mealtime assistance and 57 (75%) received snacks; thus, most of the gain in estimated total daily calories for the intervention group was due to snacks.'
issues.replacement: One result needs care. Among 76 residents with low intake who responded to a two-day trial of the help, 56 in 100 kept or gained weight over 24 weeks with the extra help, against 28 in 100 in usual care. But only 19 of the 76 were given help at meals; 57 were given snacks between meals. So the result cannot be credited to the 42 minutes of mealtime help.

issues.text: 38 minutes to help one person eat
issues.problem: Headline generalises one research-delivered protocol (two days, 74 residents, research staff) into what helping a person eat takes. The source line carries the study, but the headline does not.
issues.source_says: Simmons 2001: average 38 minutes per resident per meal for a two-day trial of one-to-one feeding assistance vs 9 minutes in usual care.
issues.replacement: 38 minutes of one-to-one help per meal, in one US study

issues.text: the study had no control group and no weight outcome
issues.problem: Residents were compared with their own usual-care days (3 days usual care, 2 days intervention), so 'no control group' is loose.
issues.source_says: Simmons 2001: intake estimated across 3 days of usual care and 2 days of intervention in the same residents.
issues.replacement: the study had no separate control group (residents were compared with their own usual-care days) and no weight outcome

issues.text: found the same gap
issues.problem: The two studies are not 'the same': 38 vs 9 minutes in 2001 (all residents, research staff) and 42 minutes (among the 19 residents given mealtime help) vs about 5 minutes in 2008. The direction matches; the size and basis differ.
issues.source_says: Simmons 2008: 42 minutes per person per meal (19 residents received mealtime help) vs about 5 minutes in usual care.
issues.replacement: found a similar gap

issues.text: The homes had one care aide for 6 to 11 residents on the day shift.
issues.problem: The ratio is a range across four homes as reported by directors of nursing, and applies to the 7am to 3pm shift.
issues.source_says: Simmons 2008: 'Nurse-aide level staff-to-resident ratios across the four NHs, as reported by the directors-of-nursing, ranged from 6 to 11 residents per nurse aide on the 7am to 3pm shift'.
issues.replacement: Across the four homes, directors of nursing reported one care aide for 6 to 11 residents on the day shift.

issues.text: Mealtime staffing should be planned from how many people need help and how long it takes
issues.problem: Normative statement carried without the judgement marker on X and Threads (LinkedIn marks it). Bluesky has a shorter form of the same sentence.
issues.source_says: Judgement, consistent with Simmons 2001 conclusion on staffing; not a study finding.
issues.replacement: We should plan mealtime staffing from how many people need help and how long it takes

issues.text: Care that works
issues.problem: Kicker overclaims. The evidence is one 1994 uncontrolled series of 32 people able to report symptoms plus NICE advice, which recommends the care but does not report that it works. The trials of drips are separate.
issues.source_says: McCann 1994: prospective series, no comparison group, mentally aware competent patients; NICE NG31 gives recommendations, not efficacy data.
issues.replacement: Comfort at the bedside

issues.text: In a small US study of 32 people dying in a comfort care unit, described as terminally ill with cancer, thirst and a dry mouth were relieved in every case, usually with mouth care, ice chips, moistened lips and sips of drink.
issues.problem: The headline claim covers 'the last days of life' generally, but the study had only mentally aware, competent patients who could report their symptoms, and no comparison group. People who cannot say they are thirsty (for example many with advanced dementia) are not covered. 'Were relieved' is stronger than the source's 'could be alleviated'.
issues.source_says: McCann 1994: 'Mentally aware, competent patients with terminal illnesses'; 'In all patients, symptoms of hunger, thirst, and dry mouth could be alleviated, usually with small amounts of food, fluids, and/or by the application of ice chips and lubrication to the lips'; no comparison group.
issues.replacement: In a small US study of 32 mentally aware people dying in a comfort care unit, described as terminally ill with cancer, thirst and a dry mouth could be relieved in every case, usually with mouth care, ice chips, moistened lips and sips of drink. There was no comparison group, and the people studied could say how they felt.

issues.text: In a small US study of 32 people with cancer, it worked in every case.
issues.problem: 'It worked in every case' overstates an uncontrolled series: no comparison group, only people able to report symptoms, 1994, single unit.
issues.source_says: McCann 1994, as above.
issues.replacement: In a small US study of 32 mentally aware people with cancer and no comparison group, thirst and a dry mouth could be relieved in every case.

issues.text: The authors described them as terminally ill with cancer.
issues.problem: Missing qualification that all patients were mentally aware and able to report symptoms, which limits who the finding applies to.
issues.source_says: McCann 1994: 'Mentally aware, competent patients'.
issues.replacement: The authors described them as terminally ill with cancer. All were mentally aware and able to say how they felt, so the study says little about people who cannot report thirst.

issues.text: (NICE; a small US study of 32 people with cancer)
issues.problem: Brackets attribute the claim that the care 'can ease' thirst to NICE. NICE advises the care; the easing comes from the small study.
issues.source_says: NG31 as read: recommendations on mouth and lip care and drinks; no efficacy claim.
issues.replacement: (NICE advises this care; a small US study of 32 people with cancer found thirst could be relieved)

issues.text: Trials of those fluids were all in people with cancer.
issues.problem: Reports the Cochrane review's included trials as all trials ever done.
issues.source_says: Buchan 2023 (Cochrane): four included RCTs (422 participants), all advanced cancer.
issues.replacement: The trials in a 2023 Cochrane review of those fluids were all in people with cancer.

issues.text: Trials were all in cancer.
issues.problem: Same: limit to the Cochrane review's included trials.
issues.source_says: Buchan 2023, as above.
issues.replacement: The trials in a 2023 Cochrane review were all in cancer.

issues.text: The symptoms measured were fatigue, twitching, drowsiness and hallucinations, not thirst or dry mouth.
issues.problem: The four named symptoms were the primary outcome; secondary outcomes also included ESAS, delirium scales and a Dehydration Assessment Scale. 'The symptoms measured' is too broad.
issues.source_says: Bruera 2013: primary outcome was the sum of four dehydration symptoms (fatigue, myoclonus, sedation, hallucinations); secondary outcomes listed many other scales.
issues.replacement: The main symptoms measured were fatigue, twitching, drowsiness and hallucinations, not thirst or dry mouth.

issues.text: too little evidence to say whether drips improve comfort or prolong life
issues.problem: The Cochrane outcomes were quality of life and survival, not comfort.
issues.source_says: Buchan 2023: 'insufficient evidence to determine whether MAH improves QoL or prolongs survival'.
issues.replacement: too little evidence to say whether drips improve quality of life or prolong life

issues.text: NICE advises helping the person drink if they want to,
issues.problem: Guidance is from 2015 and could not be checked for updates; X and Threads give no date.
issues.source_says: NICE NG31 (2015) as read in Hodgkinson, Clin Med 2016; currency not checked.
issues.replacement: NICE (2015) advises helping the person drink if they want to,

issues.text: Drawing of an older woman resting on pillows in bed while her adult son sits beside her and gently moistens her lips.
issues.problem: An invented family scene with no 'illustrative' label anywhere on the visual (P03 and P10 carry one). A reader could take it as a case.
issues.source_says: Not a source issue; style rule on invented patients.
issues.replacement: Illustration, not a real person: an older woman resting on pillows in bed while an adult relative sits beside her and gently moistens her lips.

issues.text: In the largest study, pressure sores were more common with a PEG.
issues.problem: Factually wrong. The pressure sore finding comes from one study of 4,421 people; it is not the largest study in the review (the four PEG survival studies alone total 36,816 people).
issues.source_says: Davies 2021 abstract: 'Four studies with 36,816 participants assessed the effect of PEG feeding on survival time'; 'One study of PEG feeding (4421 participants...) found PEG feeding increased the risk of pressure ulcers (moderate-certainty evidence)'. Four studies totalling 36,816 means at least one had over 9,000 participants, so the 4,421 study cannot be the largest.
issues.replacement: In one observational study of 4,421 people, pressure sores were more common with a PEG.

issues.text: In the largest study, 4,421 people, pressure sores were more common in people fed through a PEG; the review rated this moderate certainty and called the increase small.
issues.problem: Factually wrong. The pressure sore finding comes from one study of 4,421 people; it is not the largest study in the review (the four PEG survival studies alone total 36,816 people). 'Called the increase small' also quotes only the plain-language summary; the abstract's conclusion says 'a clinically significant risk of pressure ulcers'.
issues.source_says: Davies 2021 abstract: 'Four studies with 36,816 participants assessed the effect of PEG feeding on survival time'; 'One study of PEG feeding (4421 participants...) found PEG feeding increased the risk of pressure ulcers (moderate-certainty evidence)'. Four studies totalling 36,816 means at least one had over 9,000 participants, so the 4,421 study cannot be the largest.
issues.replacement: In one observational study of 4,421 people, pressure sores were more common in people fed through a PEG; the review rated this moderate certainty, the only finding it rated above low.

issues.text: More pressure sores with PEG in the largest study
issues.problem: Factually wrong. The pressure sore finding comes from one study of 4,421 people; it is not the largest study in the review (the four PEG survival studies alone total 36,816 people).
issues.source_says: Davies 2021 abstract: 'Four studies with 36,816 participants assessed the effect of PEG feeding on survival time'; 'One study of PEG feeding (4421 participants...) found PEG feeding increased the risk of pressure ulcers (moderate-certainty evidence)'. Four studies totalling 36,816 means at least one had over 9,000 participants, so the 4,421 study cannot be the largest.
issues.replacement: More pressure sores with PEG in one study of 4,421 people

issues.text: more pressure sores in the largest study
issues.problem: Factually wrong. The pressure sore finding comes from one study of 4,421 people; it is not the largest study in the review (the four PEG survival studies alone total 36,816 people).
issues.source_says: Davies 2021 abstract: 'Four studies with 36,816 participants assessed the effect of PEG feeding on survival time'; 'One study of PEG feeding (4421 participants...) found PEG feeding increased the risk of pressure ulcers (moderate-certainty evidence)'. Four studies totalling 36,816 means at least one had over 9,000 participants, so the 4,421 study cannot be the largest.

issues.text: In 14 observational studies, PEG tubes (a tube into the stomach through the skin) did not show longer survival, with low certainty.
issues.problem: Wrong denominator. The PEG survival result comes from 4 of the 14 studies; the others covered other tube types or other outcomes.
issues.source_says: Davies 2021: 'Four studies with 36,816 participants assessed the effect of PEG feeding on survival time. None found any evidence of effects on survival time (low-certainty evidence).'
issues.replacement: In four of the 14 observational studies (36,816 people), PEG tubes (a tube into the stomach through the skin) did not show longer survival, with low certainty.

issues.text: Guidance recommends careful hand feeding: regular offers of food, stopping at distress, mouth care, talking and touch.
issues.problem: Misattribution. The AGS recommends careful hand feeding but does not list these steps. The list comes from Palecek 2010, an expert proposal ('comfort feeding only'), and is untested.
issues.source_says: AGS 2014: 'Careful hand feeding should be offered'. Palecek 2010: individualised plan with regular feeding, stopping at distress, mouth care, speaking and touch; expert-proposed, not an outcome study.
issues.replacement: Guidance recommends careful hand feeding. One expert proposal describes it as regular offers of food, stopping at distress, then mouth care, talking and touch. It has not been tested.

issues.text: US and European guidance advises against tubes in severe dementia and recommends careful hand feeding.
issues.problem: Blurs two documents. AGS 2014 advises against tubes and recommends careful hand feeding; ESPEN 2024 says tube feeding is not an option in severe dementia and recommends supporting oral intake, without that phrase.
issues.source_says: AGS 2014 as above. ESPEN 2024: 'Enteral and parenteral nutrition and hydration are temporary options in patients with mild or moderate dementia, but not in severe dementia or in the terminal phase of life.'
issues.replacement: US guidance (AGS, 2014) advises against tubes in advanced dementia and recommends careful hand feeding. European guidance (ESPEN, 2024) says tube feeding is not an option in severe dementia.

issues.text: It focuses on comfort and will usually not stop weight loss.
issues.problem: Source is one hypothetical dialogue saying the plan is 'unlikely to keep her from losing weight'; 'will usually not' states a frequency nobody measured.
issues.source_says: Palecek 2010: 'places a premium on her comfort during meals but is unlikely to keep her from losing weight'.
issues.replacement: It focuses on comfort and is unlikely to stop weight loss.

issues.text: Will usually not stop weight loss
issues.problem: Same as LinkedIn.
issues.source_says: Palecek 2010, as above.
issues.replacement: Is unlikely to stop weight loss

issues.text: Careful hand feeding: what it involves
issues.problem: The panel lists steps from an expert proposal with no label saying it is untested; the LinkedIn text says so but the visual does not.
issues.source_says: Palecek 2010: expert description of a care approach, not an outcome study.
issues.replacement: Careful hand feeding: what it involves (expert-proposed, not tested)

issues.text: Urine colour, a dry mouth and thirst each fail as a single test for dehydration in people aged 65 and over.
issues.problem: Headline drops the scope: the review covers water-loss (low-intake) dehydration, not dehydration from vomiting, diarrhoea or bleeding. Only the Threads version says 'from too little drinking' in the opening line.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 Cochrane: tests for water-loss (impending or current) dehydration in people aged 65+.
issues.replacement: Urine colour, a dry mouth and thirst each fail as a single test for dehydration from too little drinking in people aged 65 and over.

issues.text: In 188 UK care home residents, 1 in 5 were dehydrated on a blood test, and thirst was not linked with it.
issues.problem: 'Dehydrated' here means serum osmolality over 300 mOsm/kg, not the 295 cut-off described elsewhere in the LinkedIn post and visual; and the exclusion of people with heart or kidney failure is missing on X.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 DRIE: 188 residents of UK long-term care without heart or renal failure; 20% dehydrated (serum osmolality >300 mOsm/kg); thirst not associated.
issues.replacement: In 188 UK care home residents (people with heart or kidney failure excluded), 1 in 5 had a blood osmolality over 300 mOsm/kg, the level counted as dehydrated, and thirst was not linked with it.

issues.text: 1 in 5 were dehydrated on that blood test.
issues.problem: The preceding paragraph says 295 or more meant starting or present dehydration; the DRIE 1 in 5 uses over 300 only, so 'that blood test' misstates the threshold.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 DRIE: serum osmolality >300 mOsm/kg.
issues.replacement: 1 in 5 had a serum osmolality over 300 mOsm/kg, the level counted as current dehydration.

issues.text: In 188 UK care home residents, 1 in 5 were dehydrated on a blood test; thirst was not linked with it.
issues.problem: Same threshold and exclusion omission.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: In 188 UK care home residents (people with heart or kidney failure excluded), 1 in 5 had a blood osmolality over 300 mOsm/kg, the level counted as dehydrated; thirst was not linked with it.

issues.text: At a cut-point of 295 mOsm/L its sensitivity was 85% and specificity 59%: it picks up most dehydrated people and also flags many who are not.
issues.problem: House style asks for absolute 'N in 100' wording. Also does not say that 'dehydrated' for this accuracy figure means measured osmolality over 300 mOsm/kg.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 BMJ Open: 19% dehydrated (>300 mOsm/kg); cut-point 295 mOsm/L: sensitivity 85%, specificity 59%.
issues.replacement: At a cut-point of 295 mOsm/L it picked up about 85 in 100 people who were dehydrated (measured osmolality over 300) and wrongly flagged about 41 in 100 who were not.

issues.text: At 295 mOsm/L or more: sensitivity 85%, specificity 59%
issues.problem: Jargon and not in 'N in 100' form; same as LinkedIn. Alt text repeats it.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: At 295 mOsm/L or more: picks up about 85 in 100 dehydrated people; flags about 41 in 100 who are not

issues.text: More useful
issues.problem: Column header puts the missed-drinks sign (one study of 71, 95% CI for sensitivity 0.59 to 1.00, unconfirmed) and a screening equation under 'More useful', which reads as validated. The Cochrane review says no test was consistently useful in more than one study.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 Cochrane: 'No test was consistently useful in more than one study'; 'Promising tests ... need to be further assessed'.
issues.replacement: Reference test, screen, and a sign to watch

issues.text: check or calculate osmolality
issues.problem: Osmolality is measured; the equation gives osmolarity.
issues.source_says: Hooper 2015 BMJ Open: calculated osmolarity vs directly measured osmolality.
issues.replacement: check osmolality or calculate osmolarity

issues.text: Small detail, real effect
issues.problem: Kicker asserts an effect. No source measured the effect of smell loss on eating in this post, and the flavour-enhancement trials were mixed.
issues.source_says: Murphy 2002 is a prevalence study; Mathey 2001 and Essed 2007 gave opposite results.
issues.replacement: Small detail, worth checking

issues.text: Things to try, with mixed evidence behind them: stronger flavours, a sauce, herbs or a squeeze of lemon.
issues.problem: Implies mixed trial evidence exists for sauces, herbs and lemon. The two trials tested commercial flavour enhancers (and MSG) in Dutch nursing homes, not these foods.
issues.source_says: Mathey 2001 (+1.1 kg vs -0.3 kg) and Essed 2007 (no difference in intake or weight): commercial flavour enhancers or MSG added to cooked meals.
issues.replacement: Things to try, though none has been tested: stronger flavours, a sauce, herbs or a squeeze of lemon. Two trials of commercial flavour enhancers in Dutch nursing homes gave mixed results.

issues.text: Things to try, evidence mixed: stronger flavours, sauces, herbs, lemon.
issues.problem: Same as X.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Things to try, though untested: stronger flavours, sauces, herbs, lemon. Two trials of commercial flavour enhancers gave mixed results.

issues.text: Try stronger flavours (evidence mixed)
issues.problem: Same as X.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Try stronger flavours (untested; trials of flavour enhancers were mixed)

issues.text: Evidence on adding flavour is mixed
issues.problem: Same as X; alt text repeats it ('Try stronger flavours; evidence is mixed').
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Herbs, sauces and lemon are untested. Two trials of commercial flavour enhancers gave mixed results

issues.text: Age, illness, medicines, smoking and a blocked nose can all weaken it.
issues.problem: Causal verb for associations: smoking and nasal congestion were associated with impairment in a cross-sectional study.
issues.source_says: Murphy 2002: 'Current smoking, stroke, epilepsy, and nasal congestion or upper respiratory tract infection were also associated with increased prevalence of olfactory impairment.'
issues.replacement: Age, illness, medicines, smoking and a blocked nose are all linked with a weaker sense of smell.

issues.text: Smell and taste can fade with age, but illness, medicines, smoking and a blocked nose can also cause or worsen it.
issues.problem: Same causal wording for cross-sectional associations.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Smell and taste can fade with age. Illness, medicines, smoking and a blocked nose are also linked with a weaker sense of smell.

issues.text: A US study tested the sense of smell of 2,491 people aged 53 to 97.
issues.problem: The study was one Wisconsin town, tested 1998 to 2000; X, Threads and Bluesky present it as 'a US study'. LinkedIn carries the limit.
issues.source_says: Murphy 2002: 2,491 Beaver Dam, Wisconsin, residents, 1998-2000.
issues.replacement: A study in one Wisconsin town around the year 2000 tested the sense of smell of 2,491 people aged 53 to 97.

issues.text: Murphy et al., JAMA 2002 (2,491 people, US)
issues.problem: Same limit on the visual.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: Murphy et al., JAMA 2002 (2,491 people, one US town)

issues.text: Small detail, real effect
issues.problem: Kicker asserts an effect while the same visual says the link does not show cause and no trial has tested night-time removal against pneumonia.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015 is observational; McReynolds 2023 gives the advice for denture stomatitis.
issues.replacement: Small detail, worth checking

issues.text: sleeping in dentures was linked with more serious pneumonia over 3 years (a link, not proof)
issues.problem: Changes the outcome. The study counted first hospital admission for, or death from, pneumonia; it did not find more severe pneumonia.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015: 'followed up annually until first hospitalization for or death from pneumonia' (48 events: 20 deaths, 28 hospitalisations).
issues.replacement: sleeping in dentures was linked with more admissions to hospital with pneumonia, or deaths from it, over 3 years (a link, not proof)

issues.text: In a Japanese study of people aged 85 and over, sleeping in dentures was linked with more serious pneumonia. A link does not show cause.
issues.problem: Same outcome change; also omits 'living at home'.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015, as above.
issues.replacement: In a Japanese study of people aged 85 and over living at home, sleeping in dentures was linked with more admissions to hospital with pneumonia, or deaths from it. A link does not show cause.

issues.text: In a Japanese study of people aged 85 and over, sleeping in dentures was linked with more serious pneumonia; a link does not show cause.
issues.problem: Same.
issues.source_says: Iinuma 2015, as above.
issues.replacement: In a Japanese study of people aged 85 and over living at home, sleeping in dentures was linked with more admissions to hospital with pneumonia, or deaths from it; a link does not show cause.

issues.text: If you or your relative wears dentures, tell the ward staff, keep them in a denture pot, and check they are not left on a tray.
issues.problem: Practical advice presented in the evidence voice. 'Tell the ward staff' rests on one small service evaluation, and the loss data are reported losses only; no study tested whether any of these steps prevents loss.
issues.source_says: Doshi 2022 and Mann 2017: reported losses and circumstances; labelling doubted as a fix.
issues.replacement: What follows is practical advice, not a trial result. If you or your relative wears dentures, tell the ward staff, keep them in a denture pot, and check they are not left on a tray.

issues.text: Care that works
issues.problem: Misleading. The trial missed both primary outcomes (resistance and oral health showed no clear difference); only secondary outcomes (acceptance, completion, duration) improved, over 3 weeks, with research staff delivering the care. The visual's own source line says refusals continued.
issues.source_says: Jablonski 2018: primary outcomes small and not clear (d = 0.16 for resistance, d = 0.18 for oral health); secondary: twice the odds of allowing and completing mouth care, longer duration.
issues.replacement: Care worth trying

issues.text: 2. The carer comes to eye level and says what will happen.
issues.problem: 'Says what will happen' is not one of the trial's listed techniques (gestures and short one-step commands are). The panel also carries an invented spoken line.
issues.source_says: Jablonski 2018 Methods 2.3: eye level, sink and mirror, avoiding elderspeak, chaining, cueing with gestures and short 1-step commands, distraction, bridging, rescue, hand-over-hand.
issues.replacement: 2. The carer comes to eye level, calmly.

issues.text: I'm going to help you with your teeth.
issues.problem: Invented quotation in a speech bubble. It is inside an 'Illustrative example' panel but is a scripted line no source supports and is not a listed technique (explaining in short, one-step commands is).
issues.source_says: Jablonski 2018 Methods 2.3, as above.
issues.replacement: Remove the speech bubble, or use a gesture without words.

issues.text: 2: the carer crouches to eye level and explains.
issues.problem: Matches the visual text issue.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: 2: the carer crouches to eye level, calmly.

issues.text: eye level, a mirror and handing over the brush made mouth care happen more often. Refusals continued.
issues.problem: Compression: 'made mouth care happen more often' drops that the gain was in acceptance and completion per session, and omits that mouth health showed no clear difference (the primary outcomes).
issues.source_says: Jablonski 2018 abstract.
issues.replacement: eye level, a mirror and handing over the brush meant mouth care was accepted and finished more often. Refusals continued and mouth health showed no clear difference over 3 weeks.

issues.text: Care that works
issues.problem: Overclaims. One cluster trial of ten wards, in residents without dementia, tested a package. The post's own text says the benefit in dementia is not established and the trial cannot say which part helped.
issues.source_says: Nijs 2006: cluster RCT, 178 residents without dementia, 5 Dutch nursing homes; Bunn 2016: family style meals 'promising', no definitive evidence in dementia.
issues.replacement: One trial, one package

issues.text: For people with dementia, reviews list family style meals as promising, but not established.
issues.problem: Only Bunn 2016 lists family style meals as promising; the Cochrane review (Herke 2018) names no specific change as established. 'Reviews list' is loose.
issues.source_says: Bunn 2016: 'Promising interventions included: ... family style meals'; 'no definitive evidence on effectiveness, or lack of effectiveness'.
issues.replacement: For people with dementia, a 2016 systematic review lists family style meals as promising, but not established.

issues.text: Over 6 months: weight held steady (+0.5 kg) with family style meals, against 1.1 kg lost with plated meals. Quality of life held steady and fell. Residents did not have dementia.
issues.problem: (1) 'Held steady and fell' is ambiguous without saying which arm. (2) '+0.5 kg' reads as a gain; the 95% CI (-0.3 to 1.2) includes zero, and +0.5 and -1.1 differ by 1.6 kg whereas the reported between-group difference is 1.5 kg. Chart bars carry the same figures. (3) Numbers beyond the abstract (+0.5, -1.1) come from the full text, which PubMed could not return here.
issues.source_says: Nijs 2006 abstract: difference in change 1.5 kg (0.6 to 2.4) in body weight and 6.1 units in quality of life. Record (full text via Undermind): intervention +0.5 kg (-0.3 to 1.2), control -1.1 kg (-1.9 to -0.2); QoL +0.4 vs -5.0.
issues.replacement: Over 6 months: weight held steady with family style meals, against about 1 kg lost with plated meals. Quality of life held steady with family style meals and fell with plated meals. Residents did not have dementia.

issues.text: quality of life held steady and fell.
issues.problem: Same ambiguity.
issues.source_says: As above.
issues.replacement: quality of life held steady with family style meals and fell with plated meals.

issues.text: A member of staff sat and chatted at every table
issues.problem: The protocol required at least one nurse, nutrition assistant or volunteer per table.
issues.source_says: Nijs 2006 Table 1: 'minimum of one nurse or nutrition assistant or volunteer per table'.
issues.replacement: A member of staff or a volunteer sat and chatted at every table

notes: All 11 posts are fixable without unsupported claims. Cross-post pattern: the visual kickers 'Small detail, real effect' (P03, P08, P09) and 'Care that works' (P05, P10, P11) assert effects the posts' own text disclaims; replace the kickers. Not re-opened (record relied on): AGS 2014, ESPEN 2024, Palecek 2010, NICE NG31 summary, Herke 2018, Abdelhamid 2016, Siervo 2014, Schiffman 1997, Doty 2008, Shepherd 2006, McReynolds 2023, Mann 2017, Doshi 2022, Jablonski 2012. NICE NG31 currency could not be checked. DOIs in all source_reply fields match the evidence records; DOIs, years and journals of the 24 reopened sources match the citations used. No invented first-person anecdotes, religion or delirium-as-topic found; P10 and P05 visuals depict invented scenes (P10 labelled illustrative, P05 not).
